**Preferred term label**
serous demilune cell of salivary gland

**Synonyms** (add reference(s), please)
serous demilune cell — Source: Amano et al. (2012), PMID:23209333 (exact synonym)
demilune cell of salivary gland — Source: Amano et al. (2012) (related synonym)
serous crescent cell — Source: standard histology nomenclature (related synonym)
Crescents of Giannuzzi https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serous_demilune

**Definition** (free text, with reference(s), please. PubMed ID format is PMID:XXXXXX)
A serous secreting cell that is part of a salivary gland, forming crescent-shaped (demilune) caps at the distal ends of mucous acini in mixed glands. Prominent in human submandibular and sublingual glands, this cell delivers its watery, enzyme-rich secretions — including α-amylase — through intercellular canaliculi that run between adjacent mucous cells to reach the acinar lumen (Amano et al., 2012). In rodents, these cells also express neuronal nitric oxide synthase (nNOS) (Isola, 2026)."

PMID:23209333
PMID:41686279

comment:
The classic crescent-shaped morphology that gives demilune cells their name is a well-established histological feature, but must be caveated with the fixation artifact issue raised by Yamashina and others. Amano et al. (2012) describe how rapid-freeze fixation reveals a more tubular arrangement, suggesting the demilune shape is at least partly artifactual.

**Preferred term label**
basal duct cell of salivary gland

**Synonyms** (add reference(s), please)
basal ductal cell of salivary gland PMID:37446355

**Definition** (free text, with reference(s), please. PubMed ID format is PMID:XXXXXX)
A basal cell that is part of the duct of a salivary gland, characterized by an undifferentiated phenotype, expression of KRT5, and a position surrounding the striated ductal epithelium. This cell is presumed to function as a salivary gland stem/progenitor cell capable of regenerating ductal and potentially acinar cell populations (Yura & Hamada, 2023; Dong et al., 2024). In mice, Lgr5-expressing cells within this compartment demonstrate tripotent capacity, able to generate acinar, ductal, and myoepithelial cell lineages (Verweij & Clevers, 2025). Additional markers in mice include Krt14 and the transcription factor Ascl3 (Dong et al., 2024).

References:
PMID:37446355
PMID:39346911

**Preferred term label**
periductal fibroblast of salivary gland

**Synonyms** (add reference(s), please)
salivary gland fibroblast — Source: general usage in Dong et al. (2024) (broad synonym)
immunofibroblast of salivary gland — Source: Nayar et al. (2019) PMID:31213547 (related synonym )


**Definition** (free text, with reference(s), please. PubMed ID format is PMID:XXXXXX)
A fibroblast that is part of the stroma of a salivary gland, positioned in the periductal connective tissue surrounding the ductal system. This cell maintains the extracellular matrix framework around salivary gland ducts and participates in immunomodulatory signaling. In the context of Sjögren's syndrome in humans, periductal fibroblasts respond to IL-13 stimulation from epithelial cells by upregulating VCAM-1, PDPN, and ICAM-1, thereby contributing to the formation of tertiary lymphoid structures (Nayar et al., 2019; Dong et al., 2024). Single-cell RNA-seq studies have identified transcriptionally distinct fibroblast subpopulations within human salivary glands, including a CCL2-high subset with spatial proximity to ducts (Li et al., 2026).

References:
PMID:39346911
PMID:31213547
PMID:41411773

(2009), PMID:18973537; Gavriiloglou et al. (2024), PMID:39590534 (narrow synonym — refers specifically to the innermost suprabasal layer attached to the tooth surface via the internal basal lamina)

**Definition** (free text, with reference(s), please. PubMed ID format is PMID:XXXXXX)
An epithelial cell that is part of the junctional epithelium of the gingiva, forming a collar-like band around the cervix of the tooth. This cell is attached to the tooth surface via hemidesmosomes and an internal basal lamina rich in laminin-332 (LAMA3/LAMB3/LAMC2) and ODAM (Lin et al., 2025; Gavriiloglou et al., 2024). The junctional epithelium is a stratified squamous non-keratinized epithelium ranging from 15–30 cell layers coronally to 1–3 cell layers apically (Gavriiloglou et al., 2024). This cell expresses cytokeratin 19 (CK19) as a specific and constitutive marker, along with ODAM and FDC-SP, and participates in innate immune defense by producing IL-8, IL-1α, and MMP-7, facilitating the continuous transmigration of approximately 30,000 polymorphonuclear leukocytes per minute through the epithelium (Gavriiloglou et al., 2024). This cell has a high turnover rate, with complete renewal occurring every 4–6 days (Lin et al., 2025), and develops from the reduced enamel epithelium during tooth eruption, although it can regenerate de novo without this precursor (Gavriiloglou et al., 2024).

References:
PMID:39590534 (Gavriiloglou et al., 2024) — comprehensive JE bioengineering review
PMID:40723411 (Lin et al., 2025) — JE structure and molecular characterization
PMID:41331699 (Zachariadou et al., 2026) — DDR1 in JE
PMID:41143768 (Sekiguchi et al., 2025) — scRNA-seq of human gingiva

**Preferred term label**
tuft cell of parotid gland

**Synonyms** (add reference(s), please)
parotid gland tuft cell PMID:3284416; PMID:38358561 (exact synonym)
brush cell of parotid gland PMID:23209333; PMID:18062147 (related synonym)

**Definition** (free text, with reference(s), please. PubMed ID format is PMID:XXXXXX)
A tuft cell that is part of the epithelium of the parotid gland, localized to the striated ducts and never observed in acini. This cell is characterized by expression of POU2F3 and is expected to possess chemosensory function consistent with tuft cells in other tissues. Immunohistochemical analysis of normal human parotid gland tissue detected POU2F3-positive cells as a very rare population (much less than 1% of epithelial cells) within the ductal compartment, positioned on the luminal side (Hoki et al., 2024). The existence of tuft cells in major salivary glands was also supported by earlier histological studies identifying brush (tuft) cells with characteristic apical microvilli in excretory duct epithelium (Amano et al., 2012).

References:
PMID:38358561 
PMID:23209333 
PMID:35993302 
PMID:38098741

**Synonyms** (add reference(s), please)

brush cell of sublingual gland  PMID:23209333; PMID:18062147 (related synonym)

**Definition** (free text, with reference(s), please. PubMed ID format is PMID:XXXXXX)
A tuft cell that is part of the epithelium of the sublingual gland, localized to the ductal compartment. This cell is characterized by expression of POU2F3, consistent with tuft cell identity. Immunohistochemical analysis detected POU2F3-positive cells in normal human sublingual gland tissue (Hoki et al., 2024). Like tuft cells in other salivary glands, this cell is expected to possess chemosensory functions and potential roles in immune regulation and salivary secretion via acetylcholine release, as described for the tuft cell of submandibular gland.

References:
PMID:38358561
PMID:23209333

ionocyte of salivary gland

**Synonyms** (add reference(s), please)


**Definition** (free text, with reference(s), please. PubMed ID format is PMID:XXXXXX)
An ionocyte that is part of a salivary gland, localized to the ductal compartment on the luminal side. This specialized epithelial cell is characterized by expression of FOXI1 and is involved in regulating and maintaining osmotic pressure within the glandular environment (Dong et al., 2024). In normal human salivary glands, FOXI1-positive cells constitute less than 5% of ductal epithelial cells and are found exclusively in ducts, never in acini, across all major gland types including parotid, submandibular, sublingual, and minor salivary glands (Hoki et al., 2024). In mice, salivary gland ionocytes co-express Foxi1 and Ascl3 and mediate stimulus-dependent Ca2+ signaling (Uchida & Ovitt, 2026). Like ionocytes in other tissues, this cell is expected to express high levels of CFTR and possess abundant mitochondria and ion transporters (Montoro et al., 2018).

References:

PMID:41721487

**Preferred term label**
myoepithelial cell of salivary gland

**Synonyms** (add reference(s), please)
salivary gland myoepithelial cell PMID:23209333; PMID:39346911; PMID:8155903 (exact synonym)
salivary myoepithelial cell DOI:10.1007/978-3-030-72029-2_4; PMID:40837863 (exact synonym)
basket cell of salivary gland PMID:38273256; PMID:27721614; PMID:26015726 (related synonym)

**Definition** (free text, with reference(s), please. PubMed ID format is PMID:XXXXXX)
A myoepithelial cell that is part of a salivary gland, positioned between the basal lamina and the secretory or ductal epithelial cells surrounding acini and intercalated ducts. This cell adopts a stellate morphology with four to eight cellular processes around acini and an elongated form parallel to the ductal axis around intercalated ducts (Amano et al., 2012; PMID:23209333). It expresses alpha-smooth muscle actin (ACTA2/α-SMA) as a primary marker, along with p63 and aquaporin 1 (AQP1), and contracts rhythmically in response to neural stimulation to facilitate saliva expulsion from secretory acini into the ductal system (Amano et al., 2012; Dong et al., 2024; PMID:39346911). This cell also produces FGF7, which activates FGFR2b-dependent transcriptional programs essential for seromucous acinar cell differentiation (Aure et al., 2023). In mice, myoepithelial cells express SOX2 and possess regenerative capacity, contributing to acinar cell restoration during tissue repair after severe injury (Ohshima et al., 2025; PMID:40837863).

References:
PMID:23209333 
PMID:39346911 
PMID:40837863 
PMID:41271704
